not_reproducible_by_rescore: evaluation_receipt_digest, and with it the candidate/1 score_result_digest and the composite_result_digest. A re-score of these bytes reproduces the SCORES, the canonical_digest and the application_result_digest exactly; it does not return the evaluation_receipt_digest 647b58570cf50cf2... or the composite_result_digest a1e2864938db84cf... this receipt records. The cause is the replayed receipt IDENTITY, not a nonce: receipt_identity() at beancount_ledger/candidate/committed.py:875 binds rollout_id, committed_revision, submitted_text_digest, stored_bytes_digest and logical_text_digest, and deliberately EXCLUDES the PrivateReceipt's attempt_id. The archive holds the canonical stored artifact and not the original submitted text, so submitted_text_digest cannot be reconstructed from it - exactly what this note's Records section says the archive does not contain. Given an identity, these digests are deterministic.

superseded_claim.text: evaluation_receipt_digest, and with it the candidate/1 score_result_digest and the composite_result_digest: a PrivateReceipt carries a fresh uuid4 per evaluation, so a re-score of the same bytes reproduces the same SCORES and the same application digests, but never the same ledger or composite RESULT digest.
superseded_claim.why_false: The uuid4 (PrivateReceipt.attempt_id) binds nothing. receipt_identity() excludes it by design - 'The input receipt minus the attempt id: a replay of the same bytes for the same revision of the same rollout is the same evaluation' - and attempt_id appears nowhere else in the package beyond its field declaration at committed.py:775. MEASURED: scoring these identical ledger bytes twice with a fresh uuid4 each time gives the IDENTICAL evaluation receipt, ledger result and composite result digests. The OUTCOME the superseded text reports is true; its MECHANISM was false and 'never' overstated it.
